review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the `toPath`/`fromPath` abbrevs in Mathlib's FundamentalGroup file, `Path.Homotopic.pi_lift` and `proj_pi` in Mathlib.Topology.Homotopy.Product, `piAssembly_map_mk` in the local FundamentalGroupoid/Product file, `map_fromPath_mk` in the local OpenCover file, and the test file that uses these lemmas. I could not run Lean. The conflict between `piMulEquiv_symm_apply` and `piMulEquiv_symm_fromPath` is therefore a reasoned claim about which simp lemma fires first, not an observed simp failure. The claim that `piMulEquiv_fromPath` is unreachable is more solid: `piMulEquiv_apply` rewrites `piMulEquiv p g i` first, and I found no @[simp] lemma for `map` of a `fromPath (mk γ)` class on fundamental groups. The test file calls the lemmas with `rw`, `exact` and `congrArg`, so I found no evidence of downstream breakage. I left `piMulEquiv_toMonoidHom`, `piMulEquiv_naturality` and `piMulEquiv_reindex` alone; marking them simp looked unjustified.

findings.problem: This is the loop-representative form of `piMulEquiv_apply`, but it is not simp. `piMulEquiv_apply` is @[simp] and has the more general LHS `piMulEquiv p g i`. On `piMulEquiv p (fromPath (mk γ)) i`, simp rewrites to `map (ContinuousMap.eval i) p (fromPath (mk γ))` and stops, because I found no @[simp] lemma for `FundamentalGroup.map` on `fromPath (mk _)`. The file's own proof has to do this step by hand with `Path.Homotopic.Quotient.mk_map`. So the canonical form `fromPath (mk (γ.map (continuous_apply i)))` cannot be reached by `simp`. Lean would not flag this, but a user who writes `simp` on a coordinate of a represented loop gets a stuck `map eval` term.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one normal form for `piMulEquiv p (fromPath (mk γ)) i`. Either add a simp lemma `map (ContinuousMap.eval i) p (fromPath (mk γ)) = fromPath (mk (γ.map (continuous_apply i)))` (the group-level analogue of the existing `map_fromPath_mk`). Or mark `piMulEquiv_fromPath` as `@[simp high]`, or `@[simp 1100]`, so it fires before the generic `piMulEquiv_apply`. If the generic evaluation form is the intended normal form, leave it non-simp and document that.
findings.benefit: `simp` could then compute a coordinate of a loop given by a representative. Callers would not have to `rw [piMulEquiv_fromPath]` explicitly, and the shadowing between the two lemmas would be settled.

evidence.excerpt: piMulEquiv p g i = map (ContinuousMap.eval i) p g :=

findings.problem: `piMulEquiv_symm_apply` is @[simp] and its LHS `(piMulEquiv p).symm q` matches every use of `piMulEquiv_symm_fromPath`. `piMulEquiv_symm_fromPath` is not simp. Simp therefore rewrites to `fromPath (Path.Homotopic.pi fun i => toPath (fromPath (mk (γ i))))`. Mathlib's `Path.Homotopic.pi_lift`, which turns `pi (fun i => mk (γ i))` into `mk (Path.pi γ)`, is not @[simp]. So the result has no simp rule to reach the stated normal form `fromPath (mk (Path.pi γ))`. The two identities compete, and the more informative one is unreachable by simp. The reasoning assumes the generic lemma gets tried first or that no lemma finishes the job; I did not run it.
findings.proposed_change: Choose one normal form for the inverse on representatives. Either mark `piMulEquiv_symm_fromPath` as `@[simp high]` or `@[simp 1100]`, so it takes precedence on loops given by `fromPath (mk _)`. Or keep `piMulEquiv_symm_apply` simp and add `Path.Homotopic.pi_lift` to the simp set locally, or as a local @[simp] wrapper. The first option is preferable if `fromPath (mk (Path.pi γ))` is the intended normal form.
findings.benefit: `simp` could compute `(piMulEquiv p).symm` on representative loops to `fromPath (mk (Path.pi γ))`. That is the form the groupoid lemma `piAssembly_map_mk` already produces. It also removes the overlap between a simp lemma and a non-simp special case.
